title: Impact of Wage Increases under Progressive Wage Model on HDB Rental Housing Eligibility Criteria
what_it_is: Impact of Wage Increases under Progressive Wage Model on HDB Rental Housing Eligibility Criteria

sections.label: HDB public rental flat assessment
sections.summary: HDB assesses rental flat requests holistically, treats the $1,500 income threshold as a guideline, and does not raise rents during the current tenancy term.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: HDB adopts a holistic and needs-based approach when assessing requests for public rental flats, and the $1,500 income threshold is just a guideline and not a hard ceiling.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Applicants will not be rejected based on income alone, as HDB will also consider applicants' circumstances, including their household size, family support, housing budget and options.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: For existing tenants who experience wage increases, HDB will not increase their rents during the current tenancy term.

sections.label: Rent increases and home ownership help
sections.summary: HDB keeps rent increases below income increases, offers grants and schemes to help tenants buy flats, and freezes rents after signing the Agreement for Lease.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: In cases where the rent is increased, HDB will also ensure that the rent increase is lower than the income increases, so that tenants are always better off when their wages increase.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: HDB has various measures in place to help public rental tenants move to home ownership.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: These include grants such as the Enhanced CPF Housing Grant and Step-Up CPF Housing Grant, the Fresh Start Housing Scheme, priority in sales exercises through the Tenants' Priority Scheme, as well as personalised guidance on the flat-buying process from HDB's Home ownership Support Team.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Once public rental tenants sign the Agreement for Lease to buy a new flat, their rents will not increase for the rest of their stay, even if their incomes increase in the period before their flat is ready.

sections.label: Applicants above income threshold offered flats
sections.summary: About 2,700 applicants with household incomes exceeding $1,500 were offered a rental flat over the last five years.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: I will take it back to the Ministry.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: I just want to assure the Member that in fact, over the last five years, about 2,700 applicants whose household incomes exceeded $1,500, were offered a rental flat.

sections.label: Rental flat waiting time
sections.summary: The waiting time is about eight months, as shared in the answer to the September Parliamentary Question.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: As we shared in the answer to the September Parliamentary Question, the waiting time is about eight months.
